pageCache.pageTitle: King's College Taunton | Independent School in Somerset
pageCache.text:
King’s
We are a wonderfully ambitious co-educational independent school offering both day and boarding school places for pupils aged 2-18, in the heart of Somerset.
We encourage. We are courageous.
Finalist in the Independent School of the Year Awards 2025 for ‘Independent School of the Year for the South of England Region.
Encouraging more curiosity, teamwork, excellence, endeavour and risk-taking…
Preparing for a competitive future within today’s challenging world…
This is a school where every member of the community feels a sense of pride in, and responsibility to, the organisation.
Nothing is more important to a school than its culture. In a culture where high expectations are balanced by appropriate support for the individual; where effort as well as achievement is noted and valued; where individuals are inspired by those around them; where kindness, decency, and duty are lived values. This is a school where every member of the community feels a sense of pride in, and responsibility to, the organisation.
We aim to provide the best educational experience in the Southwest. We encourage you to explore our website to understand what we mean by that statement, but our wonderful school is best experienced in person, either on one of several open days throughout the year, or by contacting our admissions department. It is by seeing the College up close that the magic of King’s is made manifest.
Benjamin Evans Executive Headmaster
The Prep is a school alive with energy, warmth and laughter. Here, children are free to explore, discover, and develop into their best selves.
“My first impression of King’s College Prep was that it felt like home; a place where every child is known, valued, celebrated, and free to be themselves.
King’s is a school of wonderful contrasts: close to town, yet in beautiful countryside; a small, nurturing community with a big heart; serious about learning, yet full of laughter and joy. It’s a place where children can be children—while being gently challenged to grow into their best selves.
Through our holistic curriculum and strong pastoral care, we build confidence and trust, guide and teach, and celebrate each milestone on their journey towards independence.
There’s something very special about King’s, and the best way to experience it is to visit us. I warmly invite you to come and see it for yourself”
Heidi Berry Prep School Headteacher
King’s Highlights
At King’s, we’re incredibly proud of the academic achievements of our pupils. Achieving outstanding exam results in Somerset.
Outstanding Education in the Heart of Somerset.
Located in beautiful Somerset countryside, our independent school offers the perfect environment for learning and personal growth. King’s College Taunton combines the benefits of a traditional English private school with modern teaching methods and facilities.
Our boarding school community welcomes students from across the Southwest and internationally, creating a diverse, vibrant learning environment. As one of Somerset’s leading independent schools, we prepare pupils for success at top universities and life beyond school.
One School, Two Wonderful Sites

pageCache.pageTitle: Aims and Ethos | King's College Taunton
pageCache.text:
About AIMS & ETHOS
At King’s we seek to empower pupils to challenge themselves intellectually to learn and grow, and most importantly to develop a lifelong love of learning for it’s own sake, not simply to pass an exam.
With small class sizes, alongside exceptional learning and pastoral care focused on developing the whole child, King’s commands a strong academic reputation. That’s also because during formative years and beyond we expect and encourage curiosity, teamwork, excellence, endeavour and risk-taking.
Pupils of all ages are encouraged to embrace the rich and diverse co-curricular and hobby programmes on offer, to step out of their comfort zone and enhance their confidence to become more robust, fulfilled and content versions of themselves.
Throughout their journey with us, pupils remain grounded, respectful and open-minded to the world around them.
SCHOOL ETHOS
At King’s, we celebrate a diverse community that includes individuals of all faiths and none.
We encourage our school community to explore their understanding of themselves and the world through a rich programme of academic, cultural, sporting, and social activities.
All faiths are embraced at King’s, ensuring that pupils receive the support and freedom to practice their religious choices appropriately. Recognising the importance of religious literacy, opportunities are provided for pupils to study and explore the world’s great faith traditions in a formal academic setting.
Within our schools, pupils are always encouraged to have the courage to explore the world and its faiths, helping them to develop as well-rounded citizens ready to make a positive impact in the world.
OUR MISSION
To inspire a lifelong love of learning, creativity and courage in every child within a nurturing and joyful community. We develop confident, resilient, collaborative and compassionate individuals, through a comprehensive education and outstanding pupil support that’s enriched by innovative technologies and grounded in humanity.
Our Values
We aim, in our pupils of all ages, to inspire a lifelong love of learning through the following core values:
Community
Respect is the fundamental basis of all communities and the King’s community is no exception. We are a tolerant and nurturing community that cares about each of its members and the world around us; we are a part of society, not apart from it. Our inclusive ethos gives everyone the freedom to flourish and grow.
Inclusion, spirituality, care, compassion, empathy, courteousness, nurturing, tolerance, respect.
Courage
King’s pupils will have the courage to overcome challenges, persevere and endeavour to reach their full potential by always striving to be the best version of themselves.
Challenge ideas, independence of thought, risk-takers, resilience/try again, endeavour, freedom to take risks with learning.
Curiosity
We encourage pupils to think critically, challenge ideas and take on board different perspectives. We instil a lifelong love for learning and provide our pupils with a skill-set that will enable them to meet the as-yet unknown challenges of the future workplace.
Thinking outside the box, challenge/question ideas, independence, different perspectives, evaluate, aspiration both at and beyond school, conscientious.
Collaboration
A collaborative learning atmosphere is at the heart of all we do at King’s. We listen and work together to support each other, enabling us to aim high and succeed.
Listening, embracing new ideas, helping others, teamwork, responsible, accepting peer support, learning from others.
Creativity
Higher-order creative thinking is a fundamental part of the learning journey at King’s. By liberating imaginations from the outset, embracing a reflective, risk-taking and problem-solving approach we embody creativity and expression in all stages and areas of the curriculum.
Problem-solving, flexible, higher-order thinking, making links, experimental with new ideas, risk-taking, reflective, bold, language.

ABOUT US HEAD’S WELCOME
At King’s, we are committed to ensuring that every young person has the opportunity to unlock their potential, regardless of background or circumstance.
I am exceptionally proud to lead this wonderful school, as its thirteenth headmaster, providing continuity to the values-based education that dates to 1880. 2026 marks my 29th year in education and I have taught at some of the UK’s best schools as well as spending six years overseas.
King’s College is a special place – there is a unique culture and ethos to steward and protect. Leading King’s to its sesquicentenary and beyond requires us to husband the history and tradition of the school whilst taking advantage of the very best in modern education. The King’s DNA is one of kindness and quiet achievement – not flashy but determined to punch above its weight.
I will bring a sense of purpose, pace, and pride. I am optimistic about the future. There has never been a more stimulating time to receive an education, and by harnessing, promoting, and gatekeeping (where necessary) current educational opportunities (including AI), we will create a nurturing yet appropriately challenging space for King’s pupils.
The full boarding ethos, whether pupils are full boarders or not, is evident at King’s. It is via the ideal blend of analogue with digital life that defines boarding schools as the perfect place to build meaningful relationships across the age range, whilst also being prepared for the challenges of a fast-developing world.
Benjamin Evans Executive Headmaster
“This is a happy, nurturing school with a wide range of opportunities there for the taking, whatever your child’s interests and abilities.”

ADMISSIONS WELCOME TO KING’S
Simple & seamless: Our admissions process
Our goal is to make your admissions journey as smooth and straightforward as possible.
We’re here to guide you every step of the way as you consider joining our community. Whatever the age of your child, we have all the information and support you need to make an informed decision.
Please explore the specific requirements and timeline for your child’s entry point. We are happy to help you with any questions you may have, and to ensure your path to joining us is a smooth one.
Above all, we look forward to welcoming you to King’s.
VISIT US
We are a wonderfully ambitious co-educational day and boarding school for pupils aged 3-18, in the heart of Somerset. We encourage. We are courageous. We are King’s.
Don’t just take our word for it – visit us and discover King’s for yourself.
JOIN KING’S AT:

TRAVEL
We want to make using our school transport as convenient as possible for you and your child, and we offer a wide range of routes with multiple stops along the way. Our transport service provides an affordable way for your child to travel between school and home.
GETTING HERE
Nestled in the heart of the West Country, King’s is closer than you might think. Whether you are local to Somerset, commuting from neighbouring Devon or Bristol, or joining us from further afield.
Kings is proud to serve families across the region. With Taunton’s station just minutes away and the M5 on our doorstep, a King’s College Taunton education is within easy reach.
Our Admissions team is happy to answer any questions – please get in touch.

Nursery The Pelican Difference
Welcome to the Pelican Nursery
At the Pelican nursery, we provide a warm, nurturing environment where young children feel happy, secure, and excited to learn.
Our family-oriented approach ensures that your little one will feel valued and supported as they take their first small steps in education.
We believe children learn best when they feel safe and confident, which is why we create a caring and stimulating setting where curiosity is encouraged, friendships flourish, and individual needs are met.
Our dedicated team takes the time to truly know each child, fostering close relationships that help them thrive.
Our nursery is open all year round. We have a dedicated baby room and accept children from 6 months up to 4 years old.
Our Admissions team are happy to answer any questions – please get in touch.
“The thing that shines through time and time again is how well they know the children. That nurturing, pastoral care, and the way the children just feel like they’re part of the family.”

Our lovely setting is designed to inspire young minds, offering a wealth of experiences both inside and outside the classroom:

pageCache.pageTitle: King's Pupils Celebrate Strongest A-level Results in Recent Years - King's College Taunton
pageCache.text:
King’s Pupils Celebrate Strongest A-level Results in Recent Years
Pupils at King’s College, Taunton are today celebrating the strongest set of A-level results in recent years, with the Class of 2026 achieving an outstanding 100% pass rate with 76% A*-B grades for A-level.
An impressive 42% of A-level grades were awarded at A*-A, rising to 48% across A-level and BTEC qualifications combined.
As a result, the King’s Class of 2026 has secured places to a range of top university destinations including: Bath, Birmingham, Bristol, Cardiff, Durham, Exeter, Glasgow, Lancaster, Loughborough, Manchester, Nottingham, Newcastle, Oxford, St Andrews, Southampton, UCL, Warwick, and York. While pupils have also earned places at prestigious International universities in Canada and Hong Kong, and a sports scholarship in the United States.
Excellence across the board
Alongside these outstanding achievements, pupils delivered particularly strong results in several core academic subjects, excelling in Mathematics with 89.3% of grades awarded at A*-B as well as Chemistry (87.5%), Biology and Geography (84.6%) English Literature (75%) and History (77.8%).
Several departments celebrated outstanding success, with Art achieving an exceptional 100% A* rate, while Drama, French and Philosophy departments and all recorded 100% of grades at A*-B. Pupils completing the Extended Project Qualification (EPQ) also achieved exceptional outcomes.
Spotlight on exceptional success
This year’s results were underpinned by an exceptional group of high achieving pupils, with 12 securing three or more A*-A grades: Sienna A (A*A*A*A), Wilfred G (A*A*A), Poppy B (A*A*A*), Jago B (A*A*A), Rocco W (A*A*AA), Isabel N (A*A*A, Kritthik B (A*AA), Kate B (A*AA), Charlie H (A*A*A*), Dominic L (A*AA), Roisin O’S (A*AA), Scarlett S (A*AA). In addition, seven pupils gained the equivalent of three A*-A grades in BTEC Sport: Hugo B, Holly E, Benny J, Henry M, Samuel P, Harrison P and Sophie P.
Oliver Ellsworth, Head of Sixth Form, commented:
“I am absolutely delighted with this set of results. To say the Upper Sixth worked hard for these grades feels like something of an understatement. From the moment they first walked through the doors of the Sixth Form Centre, the leavers of 2026 were an absolute pleasure to work with. They have applied themselves tirelessly, formed lasting friendships, and approached all areas of school life with determination and inquisitiveness. I am immensely proud of what they have achieved, and I also know that this is only the start of a very bright future for them all.”
Music, Drama and Art celebrate exceptional achievement
King’s creative subjects continue to thrive, with pupils also achieving outstanding results and progressing to prestigious destinations. Poppy B will study Music and Modern Languages at Bristol, Jonathan S has secured a place at LIPA to study Foundation Acting, and Thea DB will study Film and History at Manchester, highlighting the strength of creative pathways alongside King’s academic excellence.
Another exceptional year for BTEC pupils
The strength of King’s vocational pathways was also reflected in another exceptional year for BTEC Sport, building on the department’s strong track record. Pupils gained results equivalent to 83% A*-A and have secured places at leading universities: Durham, Bath, Exeter and Birmingham, where they will study degree courses including Sport and Exercise Science, Strength and Conditioning, and Sports Rehabilitation.
Preparing pupils for the next step
Central to the success of each pupil is King’s dedicated Futures Department, which works closely with every pupil to provide personalised guidance on their next steps. The breadth and quality of university destinations secured by this year’s cohort, alongside the school’s strongest results in recent years, further underlines King’s position as a leading academic school in the Southwest.
Particularly noteworthy is the success of those applying for highly competitive courses, with 100% of Medicine applicants securing places at their chosen universities. While King’s College, Taunton continues to secure high numbers of places to read Economics, Engineering and Biomedicine, it is also pleasing to see a growing proportion of pupils choosing to pursue creative industries, social sciences and humanities including PPE, History and Psychology.
Head of Futures, Clare Lewis, commented:
“Results morning is always emotionally charged. (I always pack a handkerchief for my own personal use!). Anticipation, relief, and worry all come to a head, and as members of staff, we are so invested in our pupils that we can’t help but be swept along by the tide of emotion.
Although today is a significant milestone, the weeks and months leading up to this moment in both the Lower and Upper Sixth have been the essential building blocks. The Futures Department provides personalised one-to-one guidance and, alongside our tutor team, helps every pupil explore their post-school options.
Together, we work to instil confidence in our pupils, enabling them to make informed decisions about their futures. Regardless of the grades they received today, I am proud of every pupil, not only for their achievements but for being outstanding young people who have applied themselves to all aspects of school life.
We hope they leave us feeling empowered and excited for the future, whatever pathway they choose to follow. More importantly, they leave with the skills, resilience and adaptability needed to thrive in an ever-changing world of work and to embrace the opportunities and challenges that lie ahead.”
Headmaster, Benjamin Evans, commented:
“This morning’s A-level and BTEC results are superb. It is exciting to be joining the College at a time of such manifest academic growth and improvement.
King’s College’s class of 2026 have done themselves proud, and it is worth remembering that there are success stories throughout the grade range, not just within the highlight figures.
Academic results are a passport to the next stage of education and careers, and I could not be more pleased for this special group of OAs. A high bar has been set for year groups to come and that will act as inspiration for the pupils that follow.”
Outgoing Headmaster, Michael Sloan, added:
“I am immensely proud of this exceptional year group and all that they have achieved. These excellent results are a fitting reflection of the hard work, determination and ambition they have shown throughout their time at King’s.
Beyond their academic success, they have made a tremendous contribution to the life of the school and leave as confident and compassionate young people. I would also like to pay tribute to the dedicated King’s College teachers, tutors and support staff who have guided, challenged and encouraged them throughout their journey. Their expertise and commitment have played a significant role in helping our pupils realise their potential.
As they now move on to leading universities, apprenticeships and a wide range of exciting pathways, I have no doubt they will continue to thrive and make a positive impact on the world around them. I congratulate the Upper Sixth warmly on their outstanding achievements, and I wish them every success as they embark on the next stage of their lives.”

pageCache.pageTitle: The Arts at Pre-Prep | King's College Taunton
pageCache.text:
The Arts at King’s Pre-Prep
At King’s Pre-Prep, we introduce the arts to children in their earliest years through a variety of playful experiences.
Drama is a particular strength. Each term, our pupils have the opportunity to showcase their talents through performances: Nativity plays for Nursery and Pre-Prep, Year group assemblies where children perform for their parents, and our renowned and popular summer show involving all children from ages 2 to 7.
These productions allow our young learners to develop their confidence, creativity, and performance skills, while also incorporating music, costume, and stagecraft.
The themes of our summer shows have ranged from retellings of Maori legends from New Zealand to Royal Variety Show performances and Olympic-themed productions. Each show has a moral woven into the performance, helping to develop our pupils’ understanding of the world around them.
Music is also a core part of our curriculum.
All children from Nursery onwards receive specialist music lessons, with our Year 2 pupils learning to play the violin as part of their studies.Additionally, children who choose to learn an instrument or take singing lessons have the opportunity to showcase their progress in our informal termly concerts held in the school theatre.
Artistic expression is woven throughout the daily life of our Pre-Prep. While not a distinct subject, the children’s artwork and creative projects are often featured in our performances and displays. We believe that nurturing the arts helps to develop the whole child, fostering imagination, self-expression, and a love of learning.
So let us introduce your little one to the wide and wonderful world of the arts…

Prep THE ARTS
THE ARTS AT KING’S PREP
Here at King’s Prep we pride ourselves on our outstanding arts teaching and facilities.
Each of these departments benefit from their own specialist areas within the school, including exceptional, purpose-built facilities such as a wonderful Arts Centre, individual music practice rooms, and dedicated equipment and rooms for art and design technology.
Of course, we also have outstanding staff. Each department has a specialist teacher with infectious enthusiasm and passion for their specific arts field. The music department also offers additional lessons with extra staff for a wide variety of instruments, while drama benefits from our committed speech and drama teacher.
ART
We run a specialist Art Group for Year 7 and 8 and we also run an Arts Week for the pupils and are delighted to welcome visiting artists for these events.
MUSIC
We offer a full and varied programme of musical opportunities.
Pupils can join our school choir by audition from Year 5. In addition to our main choir, we also offer Pyrland Choir, which is open to all children in Years 3, 4, and 5.
There are plenty of music groups to participate in – Jazz Group, Guitar Group and House Music to name a few.
Our Formal Autumn and Spring concerts are very popular and provide a wonderful showcase for our musicians. Pupils can also perform at a prizegiving event and a programme of smaller informal concerts. Students also take part in the annual carol service as well as the School Big Band Day with Senior School.
DRAMA
Children in Year 4, Year 6, and Year 7 and 8 participate in performances, giving them the chance to showcase their skills in front of an audience.
Recent productions include Peter Pan, A Midsummer Night’s Dream, Oliver, and The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe.
DANCE
Pupils also have the opportunity to study ballet, and enjoy learning flamenco dancing in Arts Week.
DESIGN TECHNOLOGY
Design Technology is an inherently creative subject, allowing students to develop and bring their own ideas to life. In a world where instant gratification is often just a click away, the empowerment that comes from designing and making something unique is immeasurable
Learning skills in this area is a great opportunity for pupils who benefit from a Specialist DT Group for Year 7 and Year 8. We also run cookery sessions on Saturday mornings.

Six King’s Netballers Selected for Team Bath Performance Pathway
King’s is celebrating an exceptional year of success in netball, with six pupils earning places within the highly regarded Team Bath player development pathway.
Four pupils, Maddie H, Pippa R, Sophie S and Lizzy R, have been selected for the Team Bath ADC Exeter programme, while Netty C and Sienna J have secured places in the Junior Player Development Programme (PDP).
Team Bath’s pathway is recognised as one of the leading netball development programmes in the South West, providing talented young athletes with access to high-quality coaching, competition and development opportunities designed to support progression within the sport.
The achievements of these six pupils reflect not only their talent and dedication but also their willingness to commit to training and development alongside the demands of school life.
At King’s, pupils pursuing elite sporting opportunities are supported through the school’s High Performance Programme, which provides specialist coaching and strength and conditioning support to help athletes maximise their potential while maintaining a healthy balance between sporting commitments and academic success. This holistic approach enables pupils to thrive both in the classroom and in their chosen sport.
The selection of four players to the ADC Exeter programme and two more to the Junior PDP represents a significant achievement for the King’s netball programme and highlights the strength of the pathway available to aspiring athletes within the school.
Particularly pleasing is the breadth of talent represented across the group, with each pupil demonstrating the commitment, resilience and work ethic required to succeed within a highly competitive regional performance environment.
We congratulate Maddie, Pippa, Sophie, Lizzy, Netty and Sienna on their selections and look forward to following their continued development and success with Team Bath in the seasons ahead.

About Results and Destinations
Achieving outstanding exam results
At King’s College Taunton, we’re incredibly proud of the academic achievements of our pupils.
Our GCSE results over the past eight years reflect a consistently high standard, with an average of 96% of grades at 9-4 and 51% at grades 9-7. This showcases the balance we strike between accessibility and top performance, enabling pupils of varying abilities to excel.
Our A-Level results demonstrate sustained success, with 71.4% of grades at A*-B across eight years, and a remarkable 99.16% pass rate. This impressive academic record is a testament to the dedication and commitment of our staff and to the hard work and determination of our pupils.
GCSE Highlights
Our GCSE results show a consistently high standard over the past eight years.
A-Level Highlights
Our A-Level results demonstrate sustained success over the last eight years.
Outstanding Pupil Success at King’s College Taunton
At King’s College Taunton, success is measured not only by examination results, but by the individual journeys pupils take and the ambitions they go on to achieve. Following the strongest A-level results in recent years, members of the Class of 2026 have secured places at the University of Oxford, alongside leading Russell Group universities including Bristol, Durham, Exeter, Manchester, UCL and Warwick. Pupils have also earned places at prestigious international universities in Canada and Hong Kong, while one pupil will continue their academic and sporting journey on a scholarship in the United States.
Pupil Spotlight 2026
From Cricket Success to Durham University: Jago’s Story | A*A*A
Having joined King’s Prep, Jago’s journey through the School reflects the value of a broad and ambitious education. An Academic Scholar throughout his time at King’s, he combined strong academic performance with an outstanding cricket career.
As Vice-Captain of the 1st XI, Jago played a key role in one of the most successful periods in King’s cricket history, helping secure National Schools Cricket Cup titles at both U15 and 1st XI level. Beyond sport, he contributed to academic scholarship societies, represented the School in hockey and football, and regularly performed at school events.
Following six months at a cricket academy in Australia, Jago will begin a Psychology degree at Durham University, taking with him the academic foundations and leadership skills developed at King’s.
Medical School Success: Isabel’s Journey from King’s Prep | A*A*A
Isabel’s success in securing a place at Medical School demonstrates the strength of academic support and university preparation available at King’s College, Taunton.
Having started her education at King’s College Prep, Isabel took full advantage of life beyond the classroom, completing Ten Tors challenges, participating in CCF and representing the School in swimming and hockey. Alongside these commitments, she received tailored support through subject societies, tutoring and specialist medical school application guidance.
Her success highlights how King’s prepares aspiring medics for one of the most competitive university application processes in the UK, helping pupils develop both the academic credentials and personal qualities required for medicine.
Building a Future in Music: Poppy’s Story | A*A*A*
For Poppy, music became a defining part of her King’s experience. Through involvement in concerts, ensembles and performances, she developed both her musicianship and confidence as a performer.
Alongside serving as a School Prefect, Poppy embraced opportunities to lead, collaborate and perform, gaining valuable skills that will support her future ambitions. She will now study Music and Modern Languages at the University of Bristol, with plans to pursue a career within the music industry.
Her journey reflects the extensive opportunities available within the King’s College Taunton’s Music Department and the role these experiences play in helping pupils prepare for future study and careers.
Combining Academic Success with Elite Equestrian Performance: Sophie’s Story | BTEC D*D*D
Sophie’s time at King’s demonstrates how pupils can successfully balance academic study with high-level sporting commitments while benefiting from one of the School’s most distinctive opportunities, the ability to board at school with their horse.
Having joined King’s from Badminton School, Sophie quickly became an integral part of the thriving equestrian programme. As one of the few schools in the region able to offer onsite equestrian facilities alongside boarding, King’s enabled Sophie to keep her horse with her throughout her education, allowing her to pursue her riding ambitions without compromising her academic studies.
With access to expert coaching, dedicated facilities and the support of Head of Equestrian Mrs Selway, Sophie competed at nationally recognised events including Hickstead, Windsor and the NSEA Championships, while also enjoying significant success at regional and academy level.
Alongside her sporting achievements, Sophie developed the confidence, independence and self-belief that will serve her well as she embarks on a gap year before university. Her story highlights the unique opportunities available at King’s for pupils seeking to combine academic success with excellence in equestrian sport.
Leadership, Service, Outdoor Adventure and Sporting Excellence: Alistair’s Story | AAB
As School Captain, CCF WO2 Sergeant Major and a representative of multiple 1st teams, Alistair made an exceptional contribution to the King’s community.
His experience at King’s spanned leadership, sport, service, outdoor education and the performing arts. From helping King’s secure two National Squash Plate titles to taking on the role of Gaston in the School production of Beauty and the Beast, Alistair embraced every opportunity available to him. He also made the most of King’s extensive outdoor education programme, with experiences such as the Pringle Trophy and CCF helping him develop resilience, self-reliance, teamwork and leadership skills that will stay with him long after leaving school.
Through a combination of academic challenge, outdoor adventure and leadership opportunities, Alistair developed the confidence to step beyond his comfort zone and a commitment to supporting those around him. His journey reflects King’s belief that education extends far beyond the classroom, helping pupils develop the character, confidence and leadership qualities needed to thrive in the future.
Pursuing Medicine and High-Performance Cricket: Kritthik’s Story |A*AA
Kritthik’s success highlights the ability of King’s College, Taunton’s pupils to pursue excellence across multiple disciplines.
During his time at King’s, he secured a place within the Glamorgan U18 cricket pathway while also successfully gaining admission to study Medicine at Cardiff University. Through the support of teaching staff, sports coaches and the Futures team, he balanced the demands of elite sport with the rigorous requirements of medical school applications.
His achievements demonstrate how King’s supports pupils in pursuing ambitious goals, providing personalised guidance that enables success both inside and outside the classroom.
Pupil Spotlight 2025
Ruby Beresford-Knight | A*A*AA
Ruby was deputy Head Girl and an impeccable role model and inspiration to so many pupils, she led with courage and passion in the classroom, on the sports field, and throughout the school.
Ruby’s academic journey began at King’s Prep, where her love of Science and Maths was nurtured and encouraged. Ruby consistently threw herself wholeheartedly into every aspect of school life.
With the support of the King’s travel prize Ruby will now spend a year travelling and volunteering in South America before applying to study Economics and Maths as a joint honours degree.
Gray Sinfield | A*AA
Gray joined King’s in Year 9 from Hazelgrove on a sports scholarship alongside his twin brother Hal. As Head Boy he was an impeccable role model and inspiring leader to the school community.
School life gave Gray countless positive experiences and in his own words, his time at King’s helped shape him into the person he is today, far more than he could ever have imagined.
Gray is now enjoying a gap year before applying to The University of Edinburgh to study Politics and Economics. His plans include backpacking through India, working on a safari camp in Kenya, and taking on the Mongol Rally.
Brooke Whittaker | BTEC D*DD (Equivalent to A*AA at A Level)
Brooke went from strength to strength during her time at school, balancing training, matches, and academic commitments with impressive determination. After achieving a D*DD in BTEC Sport, she secured a place at the University of Exeter. Before beginning her degree, Brooke generously shared her skills and experience by coaching at King’s Prep sports camps—a fantastic way to inspire the next generation.
Hal Sinfield | A*A*A*
Hal joined King’s in Year 9 on a sports scholarship and has a number of proud moments under his belt, from captaining the 1st XV rugby team, playing 1st team hockey for three years, representing the school in the winning Sir Stuart Pringle Royal Marines team and leading his house to victory in the house music competition.
Reflecting on one of his most lasting memories of school, Hal recalls a moment on the sports field that stood out not for the victory on the day, but for the character building opportunity it revealed.
In his final game at the Rosslyn Park 7s rugby tournament against Cheltenham College Hal led the team with encouragement and courage. The team defied the odds, battling through two halves of extra time before being eventually knocked out. What stayed with him was not the result, but the way his teammates gave everything, played selflessly for one another, and left nothing behind on the pitch. Delivering his final team talk that day remains one of his most treasured memories.
Sofya Stygar | A*BB
From whole-school plays to LAMDA grades, tennis matches to lifeguarding qualifications, Sofya embraced every opportunity at King’s, both on and off the stage.
Sofya achieved A*BB in her A Levels and is heading to Performer’s College, part of BIMM University in Manchester, ready to take the next step in her performing arts career, with dreams of a master’s degree in London.
Cameron Wallace | A*A*A*A
From his very first days in the Nursery Cameron excelled in many areas of school life making his mark on the sports field, in the classroom and showing outstanding leadership through the CCF.
Cameron gave his all whilst at school, whether representing the team in national hockey and rugby competitions, or leading his peers to victory in the prestigious Sir Steuart Pringle Trophy. Alongside these accomplishments Cameron was awarded one of only thirty nationally awarded scholarships to Sandhurst and is set for a very bright future.

There have been many huge successes across a range of areas, with pupils achieving some superb public examination results. At A-Level, 77.4% of our pupils achieved A*-B grades, with an overall pass rate of 100%, reflecting a diverse range of abilities and a consistently high level of achievement over the past five years.
Notably, many secured places at prestigious universities such as the Ivy League University of Columbia, with 90% accepted into their first-choice or second-choice institution. The year also saw pupils being accepted into prestigious overseas Universities in Canada, Switzerland, and Hong Kong.
At GCSE, 43% of pupils earned grades 9-7 (A*-A) and 97% at grades 9-4 (A*-C), maintaining a steady trend of excellent results.
Above all, we take pride in supporting each and every pupil to maximise their potential, whether progressing to Higher Education, vocational courses, or professional careers.

Senior & Sixth Form Pastoral Care
At King’s, pastoral care is at the heart of everything we do.
Whether day pupils or boarders, every student is supported by a system designed to nurture their wellbeing and personal development.
We understand that the partnership between staff, pupils, and parents is vital, and we are committed to open, effective communications to ensure each child’s needs are met.
Our house system lies at the heart of our pastoral care, fostering a deep sense of belonging and connection among students. Day pupils are fully integrated into the boarding house structure, becoming a valued part of the house family. This unique approach creates a close-knit community where lifelong friendships are formed, and students develop a lasting sense of loyalty to the school.
Each pupil is paired with a house parent and a tutor, who work together to provide personalised support for both academic progress and personal wellbeing.
From academic challenges to friendship concerns, our house teams are always on hand to guide and support our students.
Of course, we believe in working closely with families to ensure the best outcomes for our pupils. If parents have any concerns, their child’s tutor is the first point of contact and will keep the house parent informed. For pastoral matters, house parents take the lead and can escalate issues to the Deputy Head of Pastoral Care if needed. Our open-door policy reflects our belief in transparency and approachability: parents are always welcome to reach out for support or advice.
Pastoral care isn’t just a system – it’s a reflection of our values at King’s. By fostering strong relationships, providing dedicated support, and ensuring every child feels seen and heard, we create a nurturing environment where they can thrive.
“Being a parent myself, I understand the importance of providing a nurturing environment where young people can develop into confident, well-rounded individuals. Our staff work tirelessly to create a caring community where your child can reach their full potential.”

MEET THE HEADS OF KING’S TAUNTON
BENJAMIN EVANS Head of King’s College
Benjamin Evans was appointed Headmaster of King’s in September 2026. He was educated at St Paul’s school in London and then Bedford school, where his father was headmaster. Benjamin attended Durham and Cambridge universities, receiving his undergraduate degree in single honours chemistry. Teaching and leadership positions followed at Haberdashers Aske’s, Shrewsbury, Oundle, and Wellington (in the UK), and Prince Alfred College in Adelaide, the latter three schools taking overall responsibility for the academic life of the school.
Benjamin is a fellow of the Royal Society of chemistry, with intellectual passions across the subject range. He has delivered courses in wine appreciation, art, poetry, music, and the savage beauty of American football. He lives by T H White’s line, spoken by Merlin in The Once and Future King: the best thing for being sad, is to learn something. He asserts that appreciating the beauty of our world, and the creativity of our species, is central to leading a joyful life. The power of high expectations for all and unconditional positive regard for every pupil are central to his philosophy of education.
He believes strongly in the culture of care and kindness at King’s and aims to develop further the academic pace and purpose at the College, whilst championing the warmth of a tight community. He understands the significant benefits and reassurance to parents offered by a ‘through school’ and wishes to ensure the seamless transition in all areas, from King’s Prep to the College. It is his aim for King’s to provide the best educational experience in the Southwest.
Positive, personable, with an irreverent streak, Benjamin knows that modern headship requires one to be approachable to all, as keen to listen and respond as one is to articulate a vision. Married to Victoria, whom he has known since university days. They share interests in music, theatre, literature, running, cricket and wine.
HEIDI BERRY Head of King’s College Prep
Heidi has been appointed Head of King’s College Prep from September 2025, bringing with her over 14 years of leadership experience at Sherborne Prep. Her career is supported by a master’s degree, an MBA in senior leadership, and her current role as a school inspector. She joins King’s from Sherborne Preparatory School in Qatar, where she has been Headteacher since 2023.
Educated in Jersey, Heidi developed an early love for music, particularly violin and baroque repertoire. She went on to study at the Birmingham Conservatoire before completing her PGCE at Nottingham Trent University. Her teaching career began in the Midlands, laying the foundations for what has become a distinguished path in education.
Appointed Head of Pre-Prep at Sherborne in 2010 Heidi played a pivotal role in driving change and embedding the school’s vision and mission across the wider Sherborne Schools Group. In 2022, she moved to Qatar as Deputy Head before being promoted to Headteacher in 2023. During her time overseas, she inspired staff and pupils alike, provided strategic leadership, and even learned Arabic — further broadening her international outlook.
Heidi is married to Nick, a GP and keen triathlete, and together they have three grown-up sons: Jordan, Daniel, and Sam. A passionate musician, she continues to sing and perform regularly in ensembles across the South West.
Heidi’s breadth of experience, her deep commitment to education, and her ability to lead with warmth and vision make her ideally placed to guide King’s College Prep into its next exciting chapter.
GOVERNORS
Our Council brings together a wealth of experience from a wide range of disciplines. As the Trustees of our charity, they use their expertise to safeguard the best interests of the College, its property, and its finances.
Governors may be contacted via the Clerk to the Governors, by writing: King’s College, South Road, Taunton, TA1 3LA , or by email: clerk@kings-taunton.co.uk
Jolyon has been a Governor at Kings since 2019. He is a great-great grandson of the School’s founder, Nathaniel. Born in Cornwall and schooled at Lancing College, he gained a BSc from Exeter University and more recently an MSc in Leadership from Cranfield.
He left the Royal Navy in 2025 after a 34-year career spanning helicopter operations, education, strategic engagement and project delivery. Highlights include a stint on the Royal Yacht, command of Britannia Royal Naval College and delivery of a multi-billion-pound portfolio of Government change programmes.
Jolyon’s Boardroom experience includes Trustee of UK Armed Forces Winter Sports and Chairman of the Royal Navy Winter Sports Association. He acceded to the role of Custos in July 2025.
Max attended King’s (1989-1994) and subsequently completed a Masters Degree in Engineering at Durham University.
His early career was spent at Unilever and Mars, in the UK, Germany and India. He qualified as a Chartered Accountant in 2004 and since 2013 has been a Finance Director at Dobbies Garden Centres, Tesco and latterly Screwfix.
He is currently Managing Director, UK and Ireland at Screwfix.
Outside of work, Max enjoys travelling, cooking and the outdoors.
EDUCATION AND PASTORAL, COMPLIANCE AND RISK, NOMINATED SAFEGUARDING GOVERNOR
Charis Cavaghan-Pack obtained a B.ED (Hons) at Cambridge University in 1974 and taught English and RE in the maintained sector before starting a family. She became a magistrate on the Sedgemoor bench in 1997 and served on the Bench Training and Development Committee for 11 years, and also on the Advisory Committee for nine years.
She is a Chair in both the Adult and Youth courts.
Charis has five children, three of whom were at King’s, and is married to Michael, whose last job before retirement was Director of Corporate Services at the Hydrographic Office. There are ever-increasing numbers of grandchildren, four of whom are now happily at King’s College Prep.
Charis is a communicant member of the Church of England. She enjoys reading and politics and playing bridge. Charis can be contacted in her role as Nominated Safeguarding Governor on ccavaghan-pack@kings-taunton.co.uk
FINANCE AND ESTATES (CHAIR), REMUNERATION
Since 2022 Nick has led the £6 billion Avon Pension Fund, which serves c.150,000 local government workers across Bristol, Bath and surrounding areas.
Nick was previously Chief Investment Officer of Aegon UK from 2013-2021, focused on managing workplace pensions. From 2001-2013 he was Marketing Director for wealth and pensions provider Quilter. Nick is passionate about responsible investment and champions local investment across the South West region.
Nick is an Old Aluredian and attended King’s College from 1978-1983, before going on to study Philosophy, Politics and Economics at Oxford University. Nick also gained a Masters in Business Administration from Columbia University, New York, in 1997.
APPOINTMENTS (CHAIR), EDUCATION AND PASTORAL (CHAIR), FINANCE AND ESTATES, REMUNERATION, BOARDING GOVERNOR
Marcus was educated at Bloxham School and during his career has spent 19 years as an Independent Schools’ Inspector. Before his recent retirement, Marcus was the Headmaster of the Downs Preparatory School in Bristol. His interests include reading, classic cars, windsurfing and house renovation.
REMUNERATION (CHAIR), FINANCE AND ESTATES
John was born in Devon and studied Mathematical Engineering at Loughborough University. He worked in the IT industry for over 40 years, most recently for CGI, a Canadian based global IT services organisation.
He has been responsible for the delivery of various complex IT solutions including leading the team that developed and implemented the central data services system that underpins the GB smart metering solution.
John is married with four children all of whom attended King’s College Taunton. He is an avid sports fan, particularly rugby and cricket.
FINANCE AND ESTATES, APPOINTMENTS
After being educated at Winchester College and reading History at New College, Oxford, Roger had a 40-year career in banking, which started in New York in 1980 with JP Morgan and thereafter with Cazenove & Co (later JP Morgan Cazenove), Canaccord Genuity and Peel Hunt.
The majority of his time was spent in London with Cazenove & Co. where he was a partner in the corporate finance department, advising companies in the consumer sector.
Now retired from the City, Roger is a non-executive director of the Lindsell Train Investment Trust, Chairman of the Trustees of the Imperial War Graves Endowment Fund and a Trustee of the Hestercombe Gardens Trust.
His interests are the countryside, the arts, reading and sport.
FINANCE AND ESTATES, COMPLIANCE AND RISK LEAD GOVERNOR, HEALTH AND SAFETY GOVERNOR

He has been involved in property all his working life and has lived in Somerset for the past 20 years after a number of years working and living in London.
Will is a fully qualified Chartered Surveyor and after running offices and teams for a number of international property firms he now runs his own business specialising in the sale and management of high value residential country property, estates and farms.
COMPLIANCE AND RISK (LEAD), FINANCE AND ESTATES
Helene comes from a family of OAs, her father, brother and uncle having attended King’s. She is also, reportedly, the first daughter of an OA to attend King’s (from 1978-1980). Helene was on the OA committee for many years.
After a law degree at Cambridge, Helene worked mainly in-house as counsel in various city financial institutions; primarily in wealth management and private banking. Helene is currently working as a legal advisor in the public sector.
EDUCATION AND PASTORAL, STAFF LIAISON GOVERNOR
Mark is an Honorary Assistant Bishop for the Church of England in Somerset and Devon. Born and brought up in Malpas, Cheshire, Mark was educated at Shrewsbury School, Durham University (Anthropology and English) and Trinity College, Bristol (Theology).
Over 39 years in ordained ministry, he has lived and worked as a parish priest in urban and rural Cheshire, on the Somerset Levels and Dartmoor in Devon; he has also served as Canon Missioner at Exeter Cathedral and as Bishop of Shrewsbury in Shropshire. During this time, he has had experience of being a governor at several schools and colleges.
He is left handed and his interests cover sport, fly fishing, rural affairs, butterflies, the arts and reading.
VICE-CUSTOS, EDUCATION AND PASTORAL, COMPLIANCE AND RISK, REMUNERATION, APPOINTMENTS, FILTERING AND MONITORING GOVERNOR
Rebecca is a current serving police officer and has had a fulfilling career across two police forces, Avon and Somerset Constabulary and the Metropolitan Police Service. She joined the Metropolitan Police Service in 2002, during that time experienced a varied and wide-ranging career.
She has carried numerous roles across policing directorates gaining varied experience of frontline operational roles, strategic planning, safeguarding and multi-agency engagement. Rebecca has vast experience of safeguarding, particularly that of children, young people and vulnerable people.
She has over 12 years managerial experience and believes in visible and approachable leadership and leading by example. In 2019 Rebecca returned to Somerset and since then has been working in Avon and Somerset Constabulary. Rebecca has strong ties to the school.

About OUR FUTURE
Our future: Towards 2030 and beyond
Our ongoing five-year plan (2025-2030) spans all ages from 2 to 18 years and plots our progress and goals.
Formulated with our traditional Woodard Christian roots at its heart, this is a roadmap to ensure we stay ahead in an evolving world.
Guided by strong leadership, effective governance and a clear vision for the future, King’s continues to strengthen and develop the exceptional educational experience we provide for every pupil.
GLOBAL REACH
Due to our longstanding reputation as a quality British school for nearly 150 years, we have also gained an enviable international presence:
Four King’s College Schools are currently operating internationally, in Doha, Riyadh and India, with a fifth school scheduled to open in September. There are further plans to expand our presence internationally and we have appointed a stand-alone Director of International Schools to coordinate, oversee and grow our international family.
This unique global reach means over 3,000 pupils around the world are currently educated by King’s, setting us apart and providing a huge competitive edge over the vast majority of UK independent schools. This King’s family of schools provides outstanding network opportunities for all pupils, OAs and staff.
By generating valuable annual financial returns to us here in Taunton, our international school revenue helps to insulate us, to a large degree, from any political or economic threats facing the sector.
AUTHENTIC PROGRESS
The final key element of our plan is to maintain and accelerate in Taunton the ‘one school/two sites’ philosophy – further aligning educational and operational aspects of the Prep and Senior schools, for the mutual benefit of both.
As we begin a journey of change and improvement, authenticity remains vital to our future success.
We’ll continue to strive for the best outcomes for our pupils, maximising the value we can add to their education.
Then our ultimate goal is to consolidate our reputation as one of the UK’s leading independent schools.
OUR KEY PRIORITIES
Staying at the forefront of delivering exceptional educational outcomes for pupils from 2 to 18 through innovative teaching methods via a robust teaching framework.
Ensuring unrivalled pastoral care that aids each pupil’s age and stage, with an understanding of kindness and empathy balanced with a determination to perform to their best.
Investing in outstanding facilities and specialist teachers/coaches to enhance our state-of-the-art educational offer across both school sites.
Investing further in the growth of our international family of schools to build on our success to date in this sphere.

About Our History
OUR PROUD HISTORY
King Alfred’s School, as King’s was originally named, was the fifth of Nathaniel Woodard’s schools when it opened in 1880.
Woodard chose to dedicate his new school to Alfred the Great (871 to 899), the West Country King who laid the foundations of what would become the kingdom of England. Among Alfred’s legacies was his advocacy of education. He aspired ‘to set to learning… all the free-born young men now in England who have the means to apply themselves to it’.
The school badge of the Pelican in its Piety (the parent bird drawing its own blood, taking its own life to feed its children) was chosen as a powerful symbol also found in many Christian settings. The school’s motto was chosen as Fortis et Fidelis (Brave and Faithful).
The Woodard Schools have a history of educating girls as well as boys in the Taunton area.
From 1922 to 1953 St Katherine’s, Heatherton Park (on the Taunton-Wellington road) was the sister school to King’s. Its alumni included a daughter of Emperor Haile Selassie of Ethiopia, whose son and grandson attended King’s at the same time. Girls have been educated in the Sixth Form on the King’s College site since 1968 and the school introduced full co-education in 1991.
From its inception, the school had sections for Juniors (8-12-year-olds) as well as Seniors (13-18-year-olds). The Juniors traditionally had their own accommodation, classrooms and staff centered around the ‘Junior Landing’ on the first floor of the main building.
Since 1952, our Junior School has been based in the stunning setting of Pyrland Hall, a Georgian mansion on the edge of the Quantock Hills.
Archive Gallery
OUR ARCHIVE CENTRE
Containing documents, photographs, objects and audio-visual resources relating to the history of King’s and its staff and pupils, our archive centre features displays and resources which are available to visitors by appointment on Mondays and Thursdays during term time.
Our archivist is always keen to hear from people who have school materials or recollections that they wish to add to the school archives.
